correctness.rationale: The proof establishes the invertible planar-shadow reduction, visible-chain vertex formula, fixed five-event order on a dihedral fundamental sector, elementary spherical integration, and unique optimum via a monotone ratio of two positive integrals. All dimensions, boundary cases of positive finite height, and the measure-zero generic caveat are explicit. A standalone standard-library checker reconstructed 240000 independent orthographic convex hulls for six heights and agreed with the exact probabilities within sampling tolerances; computation corroborates but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Unlike classical silhouette expectation results and modern expectation bounds, the claim gives four exact probabilities for an axial seven-vertex bipyramid, plus a unique maximum of the all-visible event. Closely indexed square-bipyramid and rectangular-pyramid results are different objects and cannot imply the pentagonal five-edge threshold ordering by a special case. Actual searches and material-read limits are recorded; definitive priority is not certified.
residual_risks: Older contour-edge studies, including the ETH Kettner–Welzl technical report, were not fully retrievable; equivalent exact laws under different terminology cannot be wholly ruled out.

Two closely indexed geometric comparison items were accessible only as abstracts, and their fuller treatments were not inspected; these summaries show different source polyhedra and no known statement implying this pentagonal result.

value.rationale: The four probabilities give a natural complete exact invariant for random shadows of all symmetric axial deformations of the seven-vertex pentagonal Johnson solid. The distinct side counts require resolving five ordered geometric visibility events, and the unique height maximizing all-vertex visibility supplies a structurally motivated optimal-shape theorem beyond a routine expected-count substitution. The exact law is directly usable for random-view statistics and shape comparison.
